# dsh-vecrecall
> **A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives your agent persistent, four-layer cognitive memory.**

The plugin mounts six `vecrecall_*` tools onto the harness tool registry, backed by
vecRecall — a lo

cal-first, four-layer cognitive memory
engine (L0 identity / L1 key moments / L2 semantic / L3 deep

retrieval) with hybrid retrieval,
meaning-level deduplication, and everything stored on your own dis

trieval) with hybrid retrieval,
meaning-level deduplication, and everything stored on your own disk.

Memory work happens in a **long-lived Python process** that holds the embedding model, so repeated
t
ool calls cost milliseconds instead of reloading weights every time.
## Install

Then restart that profile. The tools appear as `vecrecall_*`.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `vecrecall_remember` | Store a durable fact. Meaning-level dedup: near-duplicates merge instead of

piling up. |
| `vecrecall_recall` | Pure semantic search. No results means a genuine miss — that is

signal, not failure. |
| `vecrecall_context` | Build the four-layer bundle (L0/L1/L2/L3). Use at se

ssion start or when resuming a topic. |
| `vecrecall_list` | Structural listing by wing/topic. Also

how you find an id to delete. |
| `vecrecall_forget` | Delete one memory by id or an unambiguous pre

fix. |
| `vecrecall_stats` | Store size and backend health. Cheap sanity check. |

Rules worth keeping in mind: `content` is stored **verbatim**, so write self-contained statements;
`

summary` is display-only and never searched. Do not dump whole files or transient tool output into
m

y` is display-only and never searched. Do not dump whole files or transient tool output into
memory.

`embedder: 'bow'` needs nothing extra and works fully offline; `'auto'` picks sentence-transformers
when installed and silently falls back to bag-of-words otherwise.
## Security
The helper service listens on `127.0.0.1` only and requires a random per-process bearer token. It is
never exposed on a network interface. Your memory store is plain files under `dataDir`.
### Credentials

Memories are stored as plain text, and retrieval requires embedding the plain text — so once a
secre

t lands in the store there is no way to recover. Encrypting it would mean giving up search.
The only
reliable moment to act is before the write, so content is screened first:
| `onSensitive` | Behaviour |

| `redact` (default) | Replaces credential parts with `***`, keeps the rest |
| `reject` | Refuses t

he write and tells the model to strip the secret |
| `allow` | Stores content as-is (not recommended

write and tells the model to strip the secret |
| `allow` | Stores content as-is (not recommended) |

Redaction preserves the retrievable meaning: `postgres://app:s3cret@db.internal:5432/hestia` is
stor

ed as `postgres://app:***@db.internal:5432/hestia`, so "which host is the database on" still
recalls
, while the password never touches disk.

This is pattern matching, not a mathematical guarantee — it will not catch a bare password with no
k

eyword context. The durable fix is upstream: keep credentials in env vars or a vault, and let the
ag

ent reference only the variable name (`DB_URL`). The same guard runs inside the vecRecall engine,
so
CLI and skill writes are covered too.
## Compatibility

| Verified against | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 4.0.5, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 0.0.1-rc.1 |
| Type check

| `npm run check` passes (strict, erasable-syntax-only) |
| Runtime | Python bridge smoke-tested en

d to end: cold start ~23s, then 20–120ms per call |
| Live harness run | verified on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2
(desktop app): tools registered, memory written and read back |
## Troubleshooting

`import vecreca
ll`. If you installed into a virtualenv, point `python` at it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**First tool call is slow** — expected: that call loads the embedding model. Everything after it is

fast, because the process stays alive for the lifetime of the plugin. Raise `startupTimeoutMs` if
yo
ur machine takes longer than 120s.

**Recalls back almost nothing** — you are likely on the bag-of-words fallback. Install
`sentence-tra
nsformers` and start numpy-based search, or set `embedder: 'sentence'`.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`src/bridge.ts` owns the Python process, `src/tools.ts` declares the tools, `src/index.ts` is the
pl
ugin entry (`apply(ctx)`).
Uses only erasable TypeScript so a plain `node` with type stripping can load it.
